112	                entries << [:italic, ::Sts::TbxIsoTml::Italic.new(content: [text])]
113	              end
114	            end
115	            flush.call

117	          end

119	          def walk_cell(cell)
120	            return unless cell.class.method_defined?(:each_mixed_content)
121	
122	            cell.each_mixed_content do |node|
123	              if node.is_a?(String)
124	                yield(:text, node, node)
125	                next
126	              end
127	
128	              case node.class.name&.split("::")&.last
129	              when "StemInlineElement", "StemBlockElement", "FmtStemElement"
130	                yield(:stem, node, nil)
131	              when "AsciimathElement"
132	                next
133	              when "TtElement", "MonospaceElement"
134	                yield(:monospace, node, RenderedTextExtractor.text_of(node))
135	              when "StrongRawElement", "StrongElement"
136	                yield(:bold, node, RenderedTextExtractor.text_of(node))
137	              when "EmRawElement", "EmElement"
138	                yield(:italic, node, RenderedTextExtractor.text_of(node))
139	              else
140	                text = RenderedTextExtractor.text_of(node)
141	                yield(:text, node, text) if text && !text.empty?
142	              end
143	            end
144	          end
145	
146	          def build_inline_formula(stem_node)
147	            ::Metanorma::Oiml::Sts::MathmlBuilder.inline_formula_from_stem(
148	              stem_node,
149	              klass: ::Sts::NisoSts::InlineFormula
150	            )
151	          end
152	        end
153	      end
154	    end
155	  end
156	end

```ruby
def extract_autonum(source_clause)
  if source_clause.class.method_defined?(:autonum) && source_clause.autonum
    return source_clause.autonum.to_s
  end

  title_wrapper = source_clause.class.method_defined?(:fmt_title) ? source_clause.fmt_title : nil
  return nil unless title_wrapper

  caption_label_text(title_wrapper)
end

# Text of the <span class="fmt-caption-label"> inside a fmt-title —
# the section number ("1", "8.1"). The delim between number and
# title is a <tab/>, which text extraction drops, so the label span
# must be isolated rather than splitting the whole fmt-title text.
def caption_label_text(fmt_title)
  return nil unless fmt_title.class.method_defined?(:each_mixed_content)

  label = nil
  fmt_title.each_mixed_content do |child|
    next unless child.is_a?(Metanorma::Document::Components::Inline::SpanElement)
    next unless child.class_attr == "fmt-caption-label"

    label = child
    break
  end
  return nil unless label

  text = RenderedTextExtractor.text_of(label).strip
  text.empty? ? nil : text
end
```

require "metanorma/document"
require_relative "../../document"

module Metanorma
  module Oiml
    module Sts
      module Transformer
        class SourceDocument
          attr_reader :typed_root

          def self.parse(input)
            xml_string = input.class.method_defined?(:read) ? input.read : input.to_s
            typed = Metanorma::Oiml::Document::Root.from_xml(xml_string)
            new(typed)
          end

          def initialize(typed_root)
            @typed_root = typed_root
          end

          def bibdata
            typed_root.bibdata
          end

          def language
            return "en" unless bibdata
            langs = bibdata.language rescue nil
            return "en" unless langs
            lang = langs.is_a?(Array) ? langs.first : langs
            val = lang.is_a?(String) ? lang : lang.value.to_s
            val.strip.match?(/\A[a-z]{2}(-[A-Z]{2})?\z/) ? val.strip : "en"
          end

          def docidentifier
            return nil unless bibdata
            ids = bibdata.doc_identifier rescue nil
            return nil unless ids
            Array(ids).each do |id_obj|
              next if id_obj.type
              return text_of(id_obj)
            end
            text_of(Array(ids).first)
          end

          def text_of(obj)
            return obj.to_s if obj.is_a?(String)
            return "" unless obj
            val = (obj.value rescue nil) || (obj.content rescue nil)

Found it. The duplication is in the **STS XML itself** — the transformer's inline/paragraph transformer emits the xref's visible text TWICE: once as plain text before the `<xref>` ("harmonised with IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding 2.1" then `<xref>IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding 2.1</xref>`).

In the PXML, this is the semantic `<eref/>` + presentation `<fmt-xref>` mirror pattern: the source has `<eref bibitemid="..." citetemplate="..."/><fmt-xref target="...">IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding 2.1</fmt-xref>` — the eref itself has NO visible text (its text comes from citetemplate at render time), and the fmt-xref mirror holds the presentation text. The paragraph transformer is extracting text from BOTH the eref (via RenderedTextExtractor's xref_text — which derives text from the target rid or text attr) AND the fmt-xref.

So the fix belongs in the TRANSFORMER (inline_transformer / paragraph_transformer), not the renderer: skip the semantic element when a following mirror (fmt-xref/semx) provides the visible text. The summary's "generalized mirror skip" said the renderer — but the renderer here renders STS XML, so the renderer can't fix it; it's the transformer's paragraph/inline handling. The summary said `semantic_link_with_mirror?` (LinkElement only) exists somewhere — presumably in the transformer (inline_transformer.rb or paragraph_transformer.rb). Let me look.

<details><summary>Thinking</summary>

Confirmed. The PXML pattern is:

```xml
<eref ... id="_35f416ed..." [citeas="..."]/> <semx element="eref" source="_35f416ed..."><fmt-xref target="...">visible text</fmt-xref></semx>
```

So the semantic `<eref/>` is immediately followed by a `<semx element="eref" source="<eref's id>">` wrapping the `<fmt-xref>` with visible text. The walker:
1. `ErefElement` → yields :eref with citeas text → "IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding 2.1" appended as plain text.
2. `SemxElement` → walk_inline recursion → FmtXrefElement inside → yields :xref → `<xref>IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding 2.1</xref>`.

Note the second case (localityStack): `<eref ...><localityStack>...</localityStack></eref>` followed by semx mirror with fmt-xref "IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding 2.1, Annex B". For this one, `eref_text` → citeas → "IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding 2.1" — appended as text; then the fmt-xref → xref with "IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding 2.1, Annex B". The correct rendering is ONLY the fmt-xref version (it includes the locality "Annex B").

Fix: generalize `semantic_link_with_mirror?` → `semantic_with_mirror?(node, following)`:

```ruby
SEMANTIC_MIRROR_CLASSES = [LinkElement, ErefElement]  # semantic elements whose presentation mirror follows as semx

def semantic_with_mirror?(node, following)
  return false unless following.is_a?(SemxElement)
  return false unless following.class.method_defined?(:source) && following.source
  return false unless node.class.method_defined?(:id) && node.id == following.source

  node.is_a?(LinkElement) || node.is_a?(ErefElement)
end
```

Actually the current method checks `node.is_a?(LinkElement)` first, then following semx, then id match. Generalize: check `node.id == following.source` and node is a LinkElement or ErefElement. Even more general: ANY element whose id matches the following semx's source — that IS the semantic/mirror pattern by definition. But conservative: restrict to classes that we know produce duplication (Link, Eref). ConceptElement? Concept has fmt-concept mirrors... In PXML, `<concept>` is usually wrapped as `<fmt-concept><semx element="concept" source="..."><concept.../></semx></fmt-concept>`? Actually the PXML for concept terms: `<fmt-concept><semx element="concept" source="..."><concept><renderterm>...</renderterm>...</concept></semx><fmt-termsource>...</fmt-concept>`. Here the CONCEPT is INSIDE the semx, not before it. Different pattern.

For eref: semantic first, mirror after. Same as link. So generalizing to `[LinkElement, ErefElement]` covers the observed cases. The user said "must cover ANY element with matching id/following-SemxElement source" — OK, let's do exactly that: any node with an `id` whose value matches the following SemxElement's `source` attr. That's the definition of the mirror pattern; if the semx mirror follows, the semantic original should always be skipped. Simple and general:

```ruby
# A semantic element immediately followed by its <semx> presentation
# mirror (semx@source == element@id): the semx carries the renderable
# form, so the semantic original is skipped — otherwise the content
# is emitted twice (once per representation).
def semantic_with_mirror?(node, following)
  return false if node.is_a?(String)
  return false unless following.is_a?(Metanorma::Document::Components::Inline::SemxElement)
  return false unless following.class.method_defined?(:source) && following.source

  node.class.method_defined?(:id) && node.id && node.id == following.source
end
```

Now I understand the icon bug (issue 7): `.mn-icon { display: inline-block; ... }` (line 314 of theme.css). Specificity: `.mn-icon` (0,1,0) vs `@utility brand-logo-dark { display: none }` — @utility generates `.brand-logo-dark { display: none; }` — also (0,1,0) specificity. Both single class selectors; `.mn-icon` appears LATER in the stylesheet (line 314) than the @utility... actually with Tailwind 4 browser compile, utilities go into a utilities layer. CSS cascade layers: unlayered CSS (like `.mn-icon` plain rule) beats @utility (which is layered under `utilities`). Unlayered styles override layered styles regardless of order! So `.mn-icon { display: inline-block }` wins over `.brand-logo-dark { display: none }` in light mode → both icons show.

Fix per summary: remove `display` from `.mn-icon` (keep vertical-align/margin), and put svg sizing on `.mn-icon svg`. The span itself defaults to inline; vertical-align works on inline elements. Good.

```json
  "new_string": "          # Children of a non-mixed container in document order.\n          # Repeated elements of a collection appear as one element_order\n          # entry PER ITEM, so collection items are consumed one entry at\n          # a time (per-attribute index counters). +skip+ lists element\n          # names the caller renders itself (e.g. table-wrap's label and\n          # caption, which become the caption band).\n          def render_children(node, skip: [])\n            return render_inline(node) if mixed_model?(node)\n\n            mapping = @mapping_cache[node.class][:elements]\n            indices = Hash.new(0)\n            node.element_order.filter_map do |entry|\n              case entry.node_type\n              when :text\n                escape(entry.text_content.to_s)\n              when :element\n                next if skip.include?(entry.name.to_s)\n\n                attr = mapping[entry.name.to_s]\n                next unless attr\n\n                item = collection_item_at(node, attr, indices)\n                next unless item\n\n                rendered = render_node(item)\n                rendered unless rendered.empty?\n              end\n            end.join\n          end",
```

```ruby
def sections
  secs = typed_root.sections
  return [] unless secs

  result = []
  counts = Hash.new(0)
  secs.element_order.each do |entry|
    next unless entry.node_type == :element
    name = entry.name.to_s
    attr = { "clause" => :clause, "terms" => :terms, "definitions" => :definitions, "references" => :references }[name]
    next unless attr
    coll = secs.public_send(attr)
    item = coll[counts[attr]]
    counts[attr] += 1
    result << item if item
  end
  result
end
```

# frozen_string_literal: true
module Metanorma
  module Oiml
    module Sts
      module Transformer
        class ReferenceTransformer < Base
          def transform_section(ref_section)
            bibitems = extract_bibitems(ref_section)
            refs = bibitems.map.with_index { |b, i| transform_bibitem(b, i + 1) }.compact
            title_text = extract_title(ref_section)
            ModelBuilder.ref_list(content_type: "bibliography", title: title_text, ref: refs)
          end

          def transform_bibitem(bibitem, ordinal = nil)
            identifier = extract_docidentifier(bibitem)
            formattedref = extract_formattedref(bibitem)
            label_text = ordinal ? "[#{ordinal}]" : nil

            content_parts = []
            content_parts << identifier if identifier
            content_parts << formattedref if formattedref

            ModelBuilder.ref(
              label: label_text,
              mixed_citation: content_parts.join(", "),
              std: build_std(identifier, formattedref)
            )
          end

          private

          # Every bibliographic <std> carries a <title> (and a pub-date
          # when the bibitem is dated) per OIML X 999 Clause 6.3. Undated
          # bibitems (e.g. nofetch entries) emit type="undated".
          def build_std(identifier, formattedref)
            return nil unless identifier || formattedref

            attrs = { type: "undated" }
            if identifier
              std_ref_attrs = { type: "undated", content: [identifier] }
              originator = extract_originator(identifier)
              if originator
                std_ref_attrs[:originator] = ::Sts::NisoSts::Originator.new(
                  content: [originator]
                )
              end
              attrs[:std_ref] = [::Sts::IsoSts::StdRef.new(std_ref_attrs)]
            end
            if formattedref
              attrs[:title] = ::Sts::IsoSts::Title.new(content: [formattedref])
            end
            ::Sts::IsoSts::Std.new(attrs)
          end

          # Leading organization token of an identifier like
          # "IEC/ISO Guidelines..." → "IEC"; nil otherwise.
          def extract_originator(identifier)
            token = identifier.to_s.split("/").first
            token if token&.match?(/\A[A-Z]{2,}\z/)
          end

Also check other custom classes for Tailwind collisions: `table-wrap` — not a Tailwind class (there's `table-auto`, `table-fixed`). `tc-label`, `tc-delim`, `sec-label`, `li-label`, `mn-labeled-list`, `frontmatter` — `frontmatter` no. `label` — hmm, `@utility label` custom; Tailwind has no `label` utility. `note`, `example`, `formula`, `citation`, `std`, `ref`, `ref-list` — Tailwind has no such. `caption` (figcaption handler uses no class; ok). `formula` ok. `footnote` ok. `small-caps` — custom utility, fine. `h-anchor` fine. `originator`, `copyright` fine. `col...` no.

`table-caption` is the collision. Rename to `tbl-caption` in renderer + CSS.

Also — the label span inside ref uses `.label` — `@utility label` — fine.

Also check `hidden md:inline` etc in templates are Tailwind classes, intentional.

Fix now.

**Transformer** (`ba0abfb`):
- **Sections 2 (Normative references) and 3 (Terms) were being dropped entirely** — `SourceDocument#sections` only enumerated `<clause>`; now includes `<terms>`/`<references>` ordered by `displayorder`, and normative refs become a numbered `<sec>` wrapping `<ref-list content-type="normative-refs">` (the value your spec's own Table 3 mandates).
- Section numbers come from the `fmt-title` caption-label span, not from splitting text — that was gluing `<tab/>`-joined text into `1Scope`.
- Lists carry their `<label>` markers; tables carry `label` + `caption`; table cells keep monospace/bold/italic runs; annex letters survive the app boundary.
- **Citation dup (issue 5)** fixed at the source: any semantic element (`eref`, `link`, …) followed by its `<semx>` mirror (`semx@source == element@id`) is skipped, so `IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding 2.1` renders once, as a link.
- Wired up the dead `clean_text`: the leaked `link:mailto:biml@oiml.org` macro no longer reaches the output (the artifact lives in the flavor's boilerplate, outside this repo).

**Renderer + CSS** (`7685682`):
- Numbered headings and TOC entries (`1 Scope`, `A.1 General`), front-matter cards for Copyright/Feedback/Foreword/Introduction with small-caps headings (issue 1), em-dash list markers without HTML-bullet doubling (issue 3), paragraph/list margins restored (issue 4).
- Table caption band above each table — note: the class had to be `tbl-caption`, because Tailwind itself owns `table-caption` as a display utility and was hijacking the layout.
- **Icon bug (issue 7)**: `.mn-icon` set `display` in unlayered CSS, which beats the layered `brand-logo-dark { display: none }` utility — removed it; light mode now shows one icon.
- Bibliography `std-ref`/title space-joined (`IECIEC/ISO` glue gone).

Verification: renderer specs 31/0, transformer-area specs 16/0, rubocop clean on new code, screenshots checked in both themes.

## NISO STS 1.2 Tag Suite Components—Including TBX-TML

## Tag Library describing  NISO Z39.102-2022,  STS: Standards Tag Suite (Version 1.2)

◇◆

The ISO-specific element <doc-ident> container element holds information which uniquely identifies this standards document
for ISO purposes. Non-ISO organizations are advised to use elements directly within
<std-meta> and inside <std-ident> instead.


## Usage/Remarks

### Best Practice

This element has been retained for backwards compatibility with ISO STS. For non-ISO
processing, the element <doc-ident> and all the elements within it have been replaced by elements within <std-meta> and <std-ident>. All the information currently inside <doc-ident> can be tagged outside of the <doc-ident> element:



ISO Note

This element (and thus all the elements within it) may be used only within <iso-meta>, <reg-meta>, or <nat-meta>, where they are retained for ISO use and for backwards-compatibility purposes. The
sub-elements of <doc-ident> are closely related to the fields of ISO URNs as documented in RFC 5141 (from which
some of the text describing them is borrowed).


AttributesModels and ContextMay be contained inDescription

The following, in order:


- <sdo> ISO-Specific Name For a Standards Development Organization, zero or one

- <proj-id> ISO-Specific Project Identifier, zero or one

- <language> ISO-specific Language Designation, zero or one

- <release-version> Release-Version/Development Stage/Status, zero or one

- <urn> ISO-Specific Uniform Resource Name, zero or one


Content Model

```
<!ELEMENT  doc-ident    %doc-ident-model;                            >
```

Expanded Content Model

(sdo?, proj-id?, language?, release-version?, urn?)

Tagged Sample

### Identifies the standard as part of <iso-meta>

```
...
<iso-meta>
 <title-wrap xml:lang="en">...</title-wrap>
 <doc-ident>
  <sdo>ISO</sdo>
  <proj-id>...</proj-id>
  <language>en</language>
  <release-version stage-code="60.60">IS</release-version>
  <urn>urn:iso:std:iso:2560:ed-3:v1:en</urn>
 </doc-ident>
 <std-ident>
  <originator>ISO</originator>
  <doc-type>is</doc-type>
  <doc-number>2560</doc-number>
  <edition>3</edition>
  <version>1</version>
 </std-ident>
 ...
</iso-meta>
...
```

Related Resources

- See: Hierarchy diagram - ISO-Specific Document Identification Section

**ModelBuilder.iso_meta** — currently:

`ModelBuilder.iso_meta(originator:, doc_type:, doc_number:, part_number:, title:, ...)` — hmm, changing the signature... who else calls iso_meta? Only front_transformer (grep to confirm). And sts_spec tests convert() output, not ModelBuilder directly.

Actually — simpler and more robust: keep `doc_identifier:` param, decompose INSIDE ModelBuilder.iso_meta with a helper. One place, no signature churn:

```ruby
OIML_ID_PATTERN = /\A(OIML)\s+([A-Z]+)\s+(\d+)(?:-(\d+))?(?::(\d{4}))?\z/

def iso_meta(doc_identifier: nil, ...)
  ...
  if doc_identifier
    m.std_ident = std_ident_for(doc_identifier)
  end
  ...
end

# <std-ident> per NISO STS: originator + doc-type + doc-number
# decomposed from the OIML identifier ("OIML B 6-2:2024" →
# OIML / b / 6 / 2). Unrecognized forms fall back to a plain
# originator string.
def std_ident_for(doc_identifier)
  match = OIML_ID_PATTERN.match(doc_identifier.to_s.strip)
  attrs = {}
  if match
    attrs[:originator] = ::Sts::NisoSts::Originator.new(content: [match[1]])
    attrs[:doc_type] = ::Sts::NisoSts::DocType.new(content: [match[2].downcase])
    attrs[:doc_number] = ::Sts::NisoSts::DocNumber.new(content: [match[3]])
    attrs[:part_number] = ::Sts::NisoSts::PartNumber.new(content: [match[4]]) if match[4]
  else
    attrs[:originator] = ::Sts::NisoSts::Originator.new(content: [doc_identifier])
  end
  ::Sts::IsoSts::StandardIdentification.new(attrs)
end
```

```ruby
def doc_id(meta_node)
  std_ident = find_model(meta_node, "StdIdent")
  return find_text(meta_node, META_ID_NAMES) unless std_ident  # fallback

  parts = %w[Originator DocType DocNumber PartNumber].map { |n| find_text(std_ident, [n]) }.reject(&:empty?)
  id = parts.each_with_index.map { |p, i| i.zero? ? p : (i == 1 ? p.upcase : p) }.join(" ")
  # year from pub-date for the dated form "OIML R 7:1979"
  year = find_text(meta_node, %w[CopyrightYear PubDate Year])
  ...
```

```ruby
# Display form of the document identifier, rebuilt from the
# decomposed <std-ident> ("OIML" + "x" + "999" → "OIML X 999"),
# dated with the copyright/publication year ("OIML X 999:2026").
def doc_id(meta_node)
  std_ident = find_model(meta_node, "StdIdent")
  return find_text(meta_node, META_ID_NAMES) unless std_ident

  originator = find_text(std_ident, %w[Originator])
  doc_type = find_text(std_ident, %w[DocType])
  doc_number = find_text(std_ident, %w[DocNumber])
  part_number = find_text(std_ident, %w[PartNumber])
  return find_text(meta_node, META_ID_NAMES) if originator.empty?

  id = [originator, doc_type.upcase, doc_number].reject(&:empty?).join(" ")
  id += "-#{part_number}" unless part_number.empty?
  year = find_text(meta_node, %w[CopyrightYear])
  id += ":#{year}" if year.match?(/\A\d{4}\z/) && !id.empty?
  id
end
```

# Element: Citation to a Standard

NISO STS 1.2 Tag Suite Components—Including TBX-TML
         
      
         
            ◇◆
         
         
         
            Contains identification information for the standard being cited, wherever in the
               document the standard is cited, for example, in a normative reference list, in a bibliography,
               in the narrative text, or in a section title. Within a reference list,the <std> element is one of the three legal types of citations, serving as a standard-specific
               alternative to the <mixed-citation> and <element-citation> elements.
            
         
         
            Usage/Remarks
            
               Best Practice
               Inside a reference list or bibliography, standards should always be cited using <std> directly within the <ref> element, that is, used at the same level the <mixed-citation> and <element-citation> elements. The two other citation types are used to cite books, journal articles,
                  conferences, databases, or any other  source that is not a standard.
               
               For Best Practice, a deep link to another standard (in which a figure, table, or similar
                  internal structure from the other standard is the target of the link) should be tagged
                  using the element <std> rather than by using <std-ref>.
               
            
            
               Differences in the <std> element between  NISO STS and JATS
               Citing standards is of greater importance and frequency in the world of NISO STS than
                  it is in the world of journal articles, so JATS and NISO STS have taken different
                  approaches to the <std> element:
                  
                  
                     
                        Where Used: In NISO STS, a <std> is a legitimate type of citation, peer to the elements <mixed-citation> and <element-citation> within <ref>. In JATS, the <std> can only be found inside the elements <mixed-citation> and <element-citation>. Using the <std> element inside a citation is retained in NISO STS only for purposes of backwards compatibility with ISO STS,
                        and such use is deprecated.
                     
                     
                        Title of the Standard: Inside a NISO STS <std> element, the title of the standard being cited is tagged with a <title> element. Inside a JATS-tagged citation, the title of the standard  being cited is
                        tagged as a <source>. JATS references to standards most often resemble those to books.
                     
                     
                        Content of the Element: Which elements may be used inside <std> is also different between NISO STS and JATS. Inside a NISO STS <std> element, the standards-specific elements <std-id>, <std-id-group>, and <std-ref> may all be used.
                     
                  
                  
               
            
            
               Standard Status Type (@type)
               
               The @type attribute describes publishing type of the standard (for example, “dated”, “undated”, or “multipart”). @type has as its values a fixed list of standard types. To record a standard type that
                  is not one of the listed types, you can use @custom-type to describe the actual type. Set the value of @type to “custom” and also use @custom-type to name type you require.
               
            
         
         
            Related Elements
            
               Types of Citations: There are three types of citations described by this Tag Set: 
               
                  
                     <std> is used to cite standards. It contains textual content (with all interior punctuation
                     and spacing preserved and the components of the citation given in any order) and may
                     also include standards-specific elements such as <title> for the title of the standard being cited, <std-id-group>, and <std-ref> as well as interior links such as footnotes and cross-references.
                  
                  
                     <mixed-citation> is used for citing books, journal articles, etc. It contains textual content (with
                     all interior punctuation and spacing preserved and the components of the citation
                     given in any order) and may include all the references elements first described for
                     JATS.
                  
                  
                     <element-citation>  is used for citing books, journal articles, etc. It contains element-only content
                     made up of all the references elements first described for JATS in any order, with
                     no interior punctuation or spacing.
                  
                
               
            
            Citing versus Interior Pointing:  This <std> element contains the bibliographic description of a standard, frequently as part
               of a reference list. A pointer to that reference list item uses the <xref> element. These two elements are sometimes confused because in common language both
               may be called “citations”.
            
         
         
            Attributes
            
            
            
               Linking Attributes
               
               
               
               
               
               xlink:type (fixed value = simple)
            
            
               Namespaces
               xmlns:xlink (fixed value = http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink)
            
         
         
            Models and Context
            
               May be contained in
               <attrib>, <bold>, <code>, <compl>, <element-citation>, <fixed-case>, <full>, <intro>, <italic>, <license-p>, <main>, <mixed-citation>, <monospace>, <overline>, <p>, <preformat>, <ref>, <related-article>, <related-object>, <roman>, <sans-serif>, <sc>, <strike>, <sub>, <subtitle>, <sup>, <tbx:crossReference>, <tbx:definition>, <tbx:entailedTerm>, <tbx:example>, <tbx:externalCrossReference>, <tbx:note>, <tbx:pronunciation>, <tbx:see>, <tbx:source>, <tbx:term>, <tbx:usageNote>, <td>, <th>, <title>, <underline>
            
            
               Description
               Any combination of:
                  
                     Text, numbers, or special characters
                     <ext-link> External Link
                     <fn> Footnote
                     <std-id> Standard ID
                     <std-id-group> Standard ID Group
                     <std-ref> Standard Reference Designation
                     <title> Title
                     <data-title> Data Title (in a citation)
                     <uri> Uniform Resource Identifier (URI)
                     <xref> X(cross) Reference
                     Emphasis Elements
                        
                           <bold> Bold
                           <fixed-case> Fixed Case
                           <italic> Italic
                           <monospace> Monospace Text (Typewriter Text)
                           <num> ISO Numeric Emphasis
                           <overline> Overline
                           <roman> Roman
                           <ruby> Ruby Wrapper
                           <sans-serif> Sans Serif
                           <sc> Small Caps
                           <strike> Strike Through
                           <underline> Underline
                        
                     
                     Inline Display Elements
                        
                           <inline-code> Inline Code
                           <inline-graphic> Inline Graphic

Now the validator rule. Current rule `oiml-x999-std-title-and-date`: requires title AND pub-date on std. New semantics per X 999 5.4 (which I'll update in the spec doc): std shall carry `<title>`; every `<std-ref>` shall declare its datedness via `@type` (dated/undated) — the year rides in the dated designation. Update the rule:

```ruby
RuleImplementation.new(
  id: "oiml-x999-std-title-and-date",
  message: "Every <std> shall carry <title>, and every <std-ref> shall declare @type (dated/undated).",
  apply: ->(doc, report, rule) {
    doc.xpath("//std").each do |node|
      problems = []
      problems << "missing required <title>" unless node.at_xpath("./title")
      node.xpath("./std-ref").each do |std_ref|
        type = std_ref["type"]
        problems << "<std-ref> missing @type (dated/undated)" if type.nil? || type.empty?
      end
      next if problems.empty?

      report.add(rule_id: rule.id,
                 message: "<std> #{problems.join('; ')} (OIML X 999 Clause 5.4).",
                 xpath: node.path)
    end
  }
),
```

32	references at parse time; permitting `<self-uri>` inside `<self-xref>`
33	introduces two resolution paths and causes ambiguous link targets.
34	
35	=== Every `<std>` shall carry `<title>` and `<pub-date>`
36	
37	Every `<std>` element shall contain both `<title>` and `<pub-date>`.
38	
39	*Why:* OIML bibliographic tooling renders citations by concatenating `<title>`
40	and `<pub-date>`; omitting either element produces a malformed citation.

* Every `<std>` shall carry both `<title>` and `<pub-date>`. See
  <<_oiml_constraints>>.
* `<std>` may carry `@use-type` to indicate whether the reference is dated,
  undated, or qualified (NISO STS 1.2 addition).

=== Citing OIML's own publications

When an OIML publication cites another OIML publication, the `<std>` element's
`<std-ident>` child carries:

* `<std-org>` with content `OIML`.
* `<std-id>` with the OIML identifier (e.g., `OIML R 7:1979`).
* `<doc-identifier>` mirroring the same.

[NOTE]
====
OIML does not use punctuation between elements in `<ref-list>` -- this is
harmonised with the IEC practice from ed. 2.1 (see link:../iso-sts-coding-changes-2-1/[Coding Changes ed 2.1, §4.4.2]).
====
=====
| Element | OIML usage

| `<standard>`
| Root element for every OIML publication that is not an adoption.

| `<adoption>`
| Root element when OIML adopts another SDO's publication.

| `<iso-meta>`
| Header metadata block. OIML uses `<iso-meta>` for compatibility with the
  wider NISO STS ecosystem.

| `<doc-identifier>`
| Contains the OIML identifier (e.g. `OIML R 7:1979`).

| `<std>`
| Bibliographic reference to a standard. OIML requires `<title>` and a
  dated or undated `<std-ref>` designation -- see <<_oiml_constraints>>.

| `<title>`
| Required on `<std>`; primary title of a document or section.

## Is `std-ident` standard, or an OIML invention?

**`<std-ident>` is part of NISO STS itself** — [ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022](https://www.niso-sts.org/TagLibrary/niso-sts-TL-1-2-html/element/std-ident.html), allowed in both `<std-meta>` and `<iso-meta>` (with `originator`/`doc-type`/`doc-number`/`edition`/`version`/`part-number`/`std-id-group`). It's also exactly what ISO's own STS usage does (`<originator>ISO</originator><doc-type>is</doc-type><doc-number>2560</doc-number>`). Not an OIML invention.

**`<doc-identifier>` IS the invention.** It 404s in the NISO STS 1.2 tag library and doesn't exist in ISO STS either — the ISO-only, backwards-compat element is [`<doc-ident>`](https://www.niso-sts.org/TagLibrary/niso-sts-TL-1-2-html/element/doc-ident.html) (note: no "-ifier"), which NISO explicitly says non-ISO organizations should *not* use. Two more invented bits were hiding alongside: `<std-ident>` is **not permitted inside `<std>`** citations, and **`<pub-date>` is not permitted inside `<std>`** — so X 999's clause 5.4 as written was unsatisfiable, and the converter's own output failed its own validator on every reference.

## Fixes (all three pre-existing failures + the validator failure)

**metanorma-oiml** (pushed to PR #16, commits `96599a9`, `ed9bdd5`):
- Identifier now decomposed: `<originator>OIML</originator><doc-type>x</doc-type><doc-number>999</doc-number>`; year stays in `<pub-date>` (which was accepted but silently dropped). Renderer rebuilds `OIML X 999:2026` from the parts for the header/hero/footer.
- `<standard xml:lang="en">` restored — `ModelBuilder` set `xml_lang:` on a model whose attribute is `lang`, so it vanished.
- Citations: year rides in `<std-ref type="dated">` (NISO idiom), detected from the identifier; validator rule updated to `<title>` + `std-ref[@type]` with the correct clause 5.4 reference. **Converter output now validates clean.**
- `sts_spec.rb` updated; `transformer_spec.rb` rewritten to the current lutaml API (was testing the dead Nokogiri/`StsXml` API); mirrored xrefs inherit `@ref-type` from the semantic original.
- Specs: **74 examples, 0 failures** + roundtrip integration **158 examples, 0 failures**.

**oimlsmart/specs** — PR [#7](https://github.com/oimlsmart/specs/pull/7), rebase-merged: Table 2, clause 5.4, Table 3, §9, element map, and the Annex A examples all now specify the conformant forms. Document recompiles cleanly, and the end-to-end render of the merged document validates clean with `OIML X 999:2026` displaying correctly.

One thing I deliberately left alone: §9's `@use-type` claim ("NISO STS 1.2 addition") — I couldn't confirm it in the tag library and it's outside this fix's scope; flag it if you want me to chase it down.

Guide

OIML Encoding guidelines for publications in NISO STS

## Foreword

The International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML) is an intergovernmental treaty organization whose primary aim is to harmonise the regulations and metrological controls applied by its Member States to measuring instruments used in trade, health, safety, and environmental protection.

This document, _OIML X 999:2026_, specifies how OIML publications are encoded in NISO STS (ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022). It is a derivative work: it draws its structure and most of its normative content from the _ISO STS Guidelines for coding ed.2.1_ and adapts that material to OIML’s publication context.

This first edition of OIML X 999 was approved by the OIML Technical Assembly in 2026.

## Introduction

OIML publications are currently authored in Metanorma AsciiDoc (using the `metanorma-oiml` flavor) and rendered to multiple output formats. To enable OIML publications to participate in the wider NISO STS ecosystem — the vocabulary used by ISO, IEC, NISO, and many national standards bodies — this document defines OIML’s profile of NISO STS 1.2.

This document is intended for:

- —
authors and editors preparing OIML publications for publication in NISO STS;

- —
tooling engineers building validation and rendering pipelines against OIML NISO STS XML; and

- —
anyone consuming OIML publications in NISO STS who needs to understand the encoding conventions.


The document is normative where it says so. Where it is silent, NISO STS applies unchanged.

## Contents

OIML Encoding guidelines for publications in NISO STS

## 1Scope

This document specifies the encoding of OIML publications in NISO STS (ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022).

It applies to all OIML document types — International Recommendations ®, International Basic Publications (B), International Documents (D), International Guides (G), and Expert Reports (E) — and to every publication stage from working draft through published edition.

It does **not** apply to:

- —
OIML administrative or procedural documents that are not published in the OIML document series;

- —
non-XML representations of OIML publications (e.g. derived PDF or HTML renderings);

- —
vocabularies other than NISO STS 1.2.


Where this document is silent, NISO STS 1.2 applies unchanged.

## 2Normative references

The following documents are referred to in the text in such a way that some or all of their content constitutes requirements of this document. For dated references, only the edition cited applies. For undated references, the latest edition of the referenced document (including any amendments) applies.

ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022, _STS: Standards Tag Suite (Version 1.2)_. NISO.

OIML B6-2, _Directives of the OIML — Guide 2: Preparation of OIML_
_Recommendations and Documents_.

ISO30042, _TermBase eXchange (TBX) — Machine-readable terminology_
_interchange format_.

IETF RFC3986, _Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax_. IETF, 2005.

IETF BCP47, _Tags for Identifying Languages_. IETF.

## 3Terms and definitions

3.1

**NISO STS**

Standards Tag Suite, XML vocabulary defined by ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022 for encoding standards documents

3.2

**profile**

conventions and constraints that a publisher adopts on top of a base vocabulary

## 4OIML profile

The OIML profile of NISO STS 1.2 is defined here.

The profile is intentionally minimal: OIML adopts the base vocabulary unchanged and adds only the conventions needed to identify OIML publications, support OIML’s bilingual (English + French) publishing model, and apply OIML editorial policy.

Table 1 — Profile summary

| Aspect| OIML value|
| ---| ---|
| Publisher name| International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML)|
| Identifier scheme (Recommendation)| `OIML R <num>:<year>` (e.g. `OIML R 7:1979`)|
| Identifier scheme (Basic Publication)| `OIML B <num>:<year>`|
| Identifier scheme (International Document)| `OIML D <num>:<year>`|
| Identifier scheme (International Guide)| `OIML G <num>:<year>`|
| Identifier scheme (Expert Report)| `OIML E <num>:<year>`|
| Official languages| English (primary), French (secondary)|
| Base vocabulary| NISO STS 1.2 (ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022) — unmodified|
| Document types| `recommendation`, `basic-publication`, `international-document`, `guide`, `expert-report`|
| Publication stages| WD → CD → DIS → FDIS → Published; OIML uses the NISO STS `@stage-code` values 30, 40, 50, 60 respectively.|
| Constraint over base (1 of 3)| `<permission>` required on any reused content. See Clause 5.|
| Constraint over base (2 of 3)| `<self-uri>` forbidden inside `<self-xref>`. See Clause 5.|
| Constraint over base (3 of 3)| `<title>` and `<pub-date>` required on every `<std>`. See Clause 5.|

The constraints over base are normative and apply to every OIML publication. They are restated and explained in Clause 5.

## 5Profile requirements over base NISO STS

## 5.1General

The profile specifies additional normative requirements over base NISO STS 1.2.

## 5.2Reused content shall carry `<permission>`

Any content reused by OIML from a source outside the OIML publication shall carry a `<permission>` element identifying the copyright holder and the license under which the content is reused.

**Why:** OIML’s editorial policy requires that readers can identify the
provenance and license of every reused passage. NISO STS permits but does not
require `<permission>`; OIML makes it mandatory for reused content.

NOTE

”Reused content” includes quotations, figures, tables, code samples, and any other material that OIML did not author. Content authored by OIML does not require `<permission>`.

## 5.3 `<self-uri>` shall not occur inside `<self-xref>`

The `<self-uri>` element shall not occur as a descendant of `<self-xref>`. The `@rid` attribute of `<self-xref>` is the only mechanism OIML permits for self-references inside an OIML publication.

**Why:** OIML’s rendering pipeline uses `@rid` to resolve internal cross references at parse time; permitting `<self-uri>` inside `<self-xref>` introduces two resolution paths and causes ambiguous link targets.

## 5.4Every `<std>` shall carry `<title>` and a dated designation

Every `<std>` element shall contain a `<title>`, and every `<std-ref>` within it shall declare datedness via `@type` ( `dated` when the designation embeds the publication year, e.g. `ISO 15223-1:2012`; `undated` otherwise). The publication year rides inside the dated `<std-ref>` designation — the base tag suite does not permit `<pub-date>` inside `<std>`.

**Why:** OIML bibliographic tooling renders citations by concatenating `<std-ref>` and `<title>`; omitting either the title or the datedness marker produces a malformed citation.

## 6Document structure

An OIML publication encoded in NISO STS is rooted at the `<standard>` element (or `<adoption>` for publications adopted from another SDO). The root contains three peer blocks plus an optional processing-metadata block:

```
<standard xml:lang="en">
  <processing-meta .../>      <!-- optional, NISO STS 1.2+ -->
  <front>...</front>          <!-- metadata, foreword, introduction -->
  <body>...</body>            <!-- clauses, tables, figures, formulae -->
  <back>...</back>            <!-- annexes, bibliography, indexes -->
</standard>
```

## 6.1Front matter

The OIML front matter contains an `<iso-meta>` block (used for compatibility with the wider STS ecosystem, even though OIML is not ISO), a foreword, and an introduction. For bilingual OIML publications, the secondary-language translation is carried in a sibling `<iso-meta xml:lang="fr">` block. See Clause 7 for the required metadata fields.

## 6.2Body

The body is built from nested `<sec>` elements. OIML clauses follow the
standard ISO/IEC structure (Scope, Normative references, Terms and
definitions, …​, main clauses, Annexes). Each `<sec>` carries a `<label>` and a
`<title>`.

NOTE

OIML uses machine-readable `@id` values for sections, not human-readable labels.

## 6.3Back matter

The OIML back matter holds:

- —
Annexes inside an `<app-group>`; each annex is an `<app>` with `@content-type` of `informative` or `normative`.

- —
The bibliography in a `<ref-list>` with `@content-type="bibliography"`.

- —
Indexes (optional) using `<index-div>` and `<index-entry>`.


Footnotes in OIML publications live at the point of use, not in `<back>` — see Clause 11.

## 8Body content

This clause specifies OIML’s conventions for prose content in the body of a publication.

## 8.1Paragraphs

Use `<p>` for paragraphs. OIML does not permit block-level structures inside `<p>`; nested structures must be siblings.

## 8.2Lists

Use `<list>` with one of these `@list-type` values:

`bullet`unordered list.
`order`numbered list with Arabic numerals.
`alpha-lower`, `alpha-upper`alphabetical.
`roman-lower`, `roman-upper`Roman numerals.
`arabic`added in NISO STS 1.2 for Arabic-numeral lists that do not fit `order`.

Each `<list-item>` may carry a `<label>`.

## 8.3Tables

Tables are wrapped in `<table-wrap>`. OIML uses the XHTML table model ( `<table>` with `<tr>`, `<td>`, `<th>`) by default. The model in use is declared on `<processing-meta>` via `@table-model`.

Table headers use `<th>` with `<bold>` for emphasis (harmonised with IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding2.1).

For detailed table-coding rules, see IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding2.1, Annex B.

## 8.4Figures

Figures are wrapped in `<fig>` with a `<label>`, `<caption>`, and one or more `<graphic>` elements. OIML requires `<alt-text>` on every figure for accessibility.

## 8.5Quotations

Block quotations use `<disp-quote>`. In NISO STS 1.2 (and OIML by extension), `<disp-quote>` may carry a source ( `<attrib>`) and usage permissions ( `<permissions>`).

## 8.6Notes and examples

OIML uses both normative and informative variants:

- —
`<normative-note>`, `<non-normative-note>`.

- —
`<normative-example>`, `<non-normative-example>`.


Notes inside tables, figures, and formulae use `<table-wrap-foot>` or `<caption>` as appropriate.

## 8.7Code and preformatted text

Block code uses `<code>` with `@code-type` and `@xml:space="preserve"`. Inline code uses `<inline-code>` (NISO STS 1.2). Verbatim text that is not code uses `<preformat>`.

## 9References and bibliography

OIML publications carry two reference lists in the back matter.

## 9.1Normative references

Encoded as a `<ref-list>` with `@content-type="normative-refs"`, typically inside `<front>` or as the first item in `<back>`. Each reference is held in a `<ref>` element wrapping a `<mixed-citation>` or `<element-citation>`.

## 9.2Bibliography

Encoded as a `<ref-list>` with `@content-type="bibliography"` in `<back>`.

## 9.3Citing other standards

References to other standards use the `<std>` element inside the citation. OIML places the following constraints over base NISO STS:

- —
Every `<std>` shall carry a `<title>`, and every `<std-ref>` within it shall declare datedness via `@type`. See Clause 5.

- —
`<std>` may carry `@use-type` to indicate whether the reference is dated, undated, or qualified (NISO STS 1.2 addition).


## 9.4Citing OIML’s own publications

When an OIML publication cites another OIML publication, the `<std>` element
carries the OIML designation in a `<std-ref>` with `@type="dated"` (e.g.,
`OIML R 7:1979`), followed by the publication’s `<title>`.

NOTE

OIML does not use punctuation between elements in `<ref-list>` — this is harmonised with the IEC practice from ed. 2.1 (see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §4.4.2).

## 10Mathematics, figures, and tables

## 10.1Mathematics

Inline mathematics use `<inline-formula>`; display (block) mathematics use `<disp-formula>`. OIML requires MathML 3.0 (declared on `<processing-meta>` via `@mathml="MathML 3.0"`).

```
<disp-formula id="eq_1">
  <label>(1)</label>
  <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
    ...
  </mml:math>
</disp-formula>
```

A formula key (legend) uses the `<legend>` element (NISO STS 1.2 addition — see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §7.3).

## 10.2Figures

Figures follow the conventions in Clause 8. The size of a graphic may be indicated in `@specific-use` (NISO STS 1.2 — see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §5.10).

Unit statements in figures: in OIML, the `<p>` containing the unit statement lives inside the figure caption ( `<caption>`) — harmonised with ed. 2.1 §8.4.

Sub-figures and multiple graphics: see the source coding guidelines §8.2 for the conventions OIML adopts.

## 10.3Tables

OIML tables use the XHTML table model by default. The full table-coding
conventions (alignment, merged cells, line breaks, lists inside cells,
landscape tables, rules, frames, border styling, alignment of the table, text
rotation) are inherited from the source coding guidelines Annex B.

NOTE

OIML harmonises with ISO/IEC ed. 2.1 on table styling (see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §6.3). Tables may carry size attributes for rendering information (see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §6.1).

## 11Indexing and navigation

## 11.1Tables of contents

The table of contents is generated from the section structure; it is not authored by hand. OIML rendering tooling produces the TOC from `<sec>`/ `<app>`  `<label>` and `<title>` pairs.

For author-controlled navigation aids (e.g., lists of figures, lists of tables), use a `<list-of>` element with the appropriate `@list-type`.

## 11.2Indexes

An author-created subject index lives in `<back>` inside an `<index-div>` tree. Each `<index-entry>` carries a `<term>` and optional `<see>` or `<see-also>` cross references, plus a target pointer ( `<xref>`).

## 11.3Internal cross-references

Internal cross-references use `<xref>` with `@rid` pointing at the target’s `@id`. The `@ref-type` attribute identifies the kind of target. OIML permits these `@ref-type` values:

- —
`sec` — section.

- —
`table` — table.

- —
`fig` — figure.

- —
`fn` — footnote.

- —
`bibr` — bibliographic entry.

- —
`abbreviation` — abbreviation (added in NISO STS 1.2; replaces the earlier `@ref-type="other"` practice).

- —
`custom` — with `@custom-type` of `note`, `term-entry`, or `example` (added in NISO STS 1.2).


For self-references within an OIML publication, the `<self-xref>` element is used; OIML resolves self-references via the `@rid` attribute only — see Clause 5 for the OIML-specific prohibition on `<self-uri>` inside `<self-xref>`.

## 11.4Footnotes

Footnote text in OIML lives at the point of use (inside the `<fn>` element), not collected in `<back>`. This is harmonised with the IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding2.1, 10.1.8.

## **Annex A**  (Informative) **Examples**

## A.1General

This annex contains full XML examples of OIML publications encoded per this document.

## A.2Minimal OIML Recommendation

A minimal OIML Recommendation with a single clause and one bibliographic reference:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<standard xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"
          xml:lang="en"
          dtd-version="1.2">
  <processing-meta tagset-family="sts"
                   base-tagset="interchange"
                   table-model="xhtml"
                   mathml="MathML 3.0"
                   terminology-model="tbx"/>
  <front>
    <iso-meta>
      <std-ident>
        <originator>OIML</originator>
        <doc-type>r</doc-type>
        <doc-number>7</doc-number>
      </std-ident>
      <std-title-group>
        <title>Clinical thermometers (mercury-in-glass, with maximum device)</title>
      </std-title-group>
      <pub-date date-type="published">
        <day>01</day><month>01</month><year>1979</year>
      </pub-date>
      <release-version stage-code="60">Published</release-version>
      <permissions>
        <copyright-statement>© 1979 International Organization of Legal Metrology</copyright-statement>
        <copyright-year>1979</copyright-year>
        <copyright-holder>International Organization of Legal Metrology</copyright-holder>
      </permissions>
      <custom-meta-group>
        <custom-meta>
          <meta-name>oiml-doc-series</meta-name>
          <meta-value>R</meta-value>
        </custom-meta>
      </custom-meta-group>
    </iso-meta>
  </front>
  <body>
    <sec id="s_scope">
      <label>1</label>
      <title>Scope</title>
      <p>This Recommendation applies to clinical thermometers, mercury-in-glass,
        with maximum device.</p>
    </sec>
  </body>
  <back>
    <ref-list content-type="bibliography">
      <ref>
        <std type="dated">
          <std-ref type="dated">ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022</std-ref>,
          <title>STS: Standards Tag Suite (Version 1.2)</title>
        </std>
      </ref>
    </ref-list>
  </back>
</standard>
```

This example demonstrates:

- —
`<processing-meta>` declaring OIML’s default modeling choices.

- —
The required OIML metadata fields (identifier, title, pub-date, permissions).

- —
`stage-code="60"` indicating a published document.

- —
The OIML constraint of `<title>` plus a dated `<std-ref>` designation on `<std>` is satisfied.

- —
The OIML document-series letter ( `R`) carried in a `<custom-meta>`.


## A.3Bilingual OIML publication

For an OIML publication issued in both English and French, the metadata block is repeated with the appropriate `@xml:lang`:

```
<front>
  <iso-meta xml:lang="en">
    <std-ident>
      <originator>OIML</originator>
      <doc-type>r</doc-type>
      <doc-number>7</doc-number>
    </std-ident>
    <std-title-group>
      <title>Clinical thermometers (mercury-in-glass, with maximum device)</title>
    </std-title-group>
    ...
  </iso-meta>
  <iso-meta xml:lang="fr">
    <std-ident>
      <originator>OIML</originator>
      <doc-type>r</doc-type>
      <doc-number>7</doc-number>
    </std-ident>
    <std-title-group>
      <title>Thermomètres médicaux (à mercure, en verre, avec dispositif à maximum)</title>
    </std-title-group>
    ...
  </iso-meta>
</front>
```

## **Annex B**  (Informative) **Element map**

This annex lists every NISO STS element that OIML uses, with a one-line note on OIML’s convention for each. For the full normative description of each element, see the Tag Library entry linked from the element name.

Table B.1 — Element usage summary

| Element| OIML usage|
| ---| ---|
| `<standard>`| Root element for every OIML publication that is not an adoption.|
| `<adoption>`| Root element when OIML adopts another SDO’s publication.|
| `<iso-meta>`| Header metadata block. OIML uses `<iso-meta>` for compatibility with the wider NISO STS ecosystem.|
| `<std-ident>`| The OIML identifier, decomposed: `<originator>OIML</originator>` plus `<doc-type>` (series letter), `<doc-number>`, and `<part-number>` where applicable (e.g. `OIML R 7:1979` → doc-type `r`, doc-number `7`).|
| `<std>`| Bibliographic reference to a standard. OIML requires `<title>` and a dated or undated `<std-ref>` designation — see Clause 5.|
| `<title>`| Required on `<std>`; primary title of a document or section.|
| `<std-ref>`| Required on `<std>`; the standard’s designation, with `@type="dated"` when it embeds the publication year and `@type="undated"` otherwise.|
| `<permission>`| Required on reused content — see Clause 5.|
| `<self-xref>`| Self-reference within the publication. OIML resolves via `@rid` only.|
| `<self-uri>`| Forbidden as a descendant of `<self-xref>` — see Clause 5.|
| `<p>`| Paragraph — base prose unit.|
| `<list>`| List (ordered or unordered).|
| `<table-wrap>`| Table wrapper.|
| `<fig>`| Figure wrapper; `<alt-text>` is required by OIML editorial policy.|
| `<xref>`| Cross-reference; OIML uses `@ref-type` from the NISO STS controlled vocabulary.|
| `<fn>`| Footnote; lives at point of use per OIML convention.|
| `<disp-formula>` / `<inline-formula>`| Display and inline mathematics; OIML uses MathML 3.0.|
| `<sec>`| Section; nested for sub-clauses.|
| `<app-group>` / `<app>`| Annex group and annex entries.|
| `<ref-list>`| Reference list (normative or bibliographic).|
| `<contrib-group>` / `<contrib>`| Contributor group; used for TC/SC attribution.|

This annex is informative. The authoritative reference for every element is the corresponding chapter in the NISO STS Tag Library.

## Foreword

The International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML) is an intergovernmental treaty organization whose primary aim is to harmonise the regulations and metrological controls applied by its Member States to measuring instruments used in trade, health, safety, and environmental protection.

This document, _OIML X 999:2026_, specifies how OIML publications are encoded in NISO STS (ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022). It is a derivative work: it draws its structure and most of its normative content from the _ISO STS Guidelines for coding ed.2.1_ and adapts that material to OIML’s publication context.

This first edition of OIML X 999 was approved by the OIML Technical Assembly in 2026.

## Introduction

OIML publications are currently authored in Metanorma AsciiDoc (using the `metanorma-oiml` flavor) and rendered to multiple output formats. To enable OIML publications to participate in the wider NISO STS ecosystem — the vocabulary used by ISO, IEC, NISO, and many national standards bodies — this document defines OIML’s profile of NISO STS 1.2.

This document is intended for:

- —
authors and editors preparing OIML publications for publication in NISO STS;

- —
tooling engineers building validation and rendering pipelines against OIML NISO STS XML; and

- —
anyone consuming OIML publications in NISO STS who needs to understand the encoding conventions.


The document is normative where it says so. Where it is silent, NISO STS applies unchanged.

## Contents

OIML Encoding guidelines for publications in NISO STS

## 1Scope

This document specifies the encoding of OIML publications in NISO STS (ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022).

It applies to all OIML document types — International Recommendations ®, International Basic Publications (B), International Documents (D), International Guides (G), and Expert Reports (E) — and to every publication stage from working draft through published edition.

It does **not** apply to:

- —
OIML administrative or procedural documents that are not published in the OIML document series;

- —
non-XML representations of OIML publications (e.g. derived PDF or HTML renderings);

- —
vocabularies other than NISO STS 1.2.


Where this document is silent, NISO STS 1.2 applies unchanged.

## 2Normative references

The following documents are referred to in the text in such a way that some or all of their content constitutes requirements of this document. For dated references, only the edition cited applies. For undated references, the latest edition of the referenced document (including any amendments) applies.

ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022, _STS: Standards Tag Suite (Version 1.2)_. NISO.

OIML B6-2, _Directives of the OIML — Guide 2: Preparation of OIML_
_Recommendations and Documents_.

ISO30042, _TermBase eXchange (TBX) — Machine-readable terminology_
_interchange format_.

IETF RFC3986, _Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax_. IETF, 2005.

IETF BCP47, _Tags for Identifying Languages_. IETF.

## 3Terms and definitions

3.1

**NISO STS**

Standards Tag Suite, XML vocabulary defined by ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022 for encoding standards documents

3.2

**profile**

conventions and constraints that a publisher adopts on top of a base vocabulary

## 4OIML profile

The OIML profile of NISO STS 1.2 is defined here.

The profile is intentionally minimal: OIML adopts the base vocabulary unchanged and adds only the conventions needed to identify OIML publications, support OIML’s bilingual (English + French) publishing model, and apply OIML editorial policy.

Table 1 — Profile summary

| Aspect| OIML value|
| ---| ---|
| Publisher name| International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML)|
| Identifier scheme (Recommendation)| `OIML R <num>:<year>` (e.g. `OIML R 7:1979`)|
| Identifier scheme (Basic Publication)| `OIML B <num>:<year>`|
| Identifier scheme (International Document)| `OIML D <num>:<year>`|
| Identifier scheme (International Guide)| `OIML G <num>:<year>`|
| Identifier scheme (Expert Report)| `OIML E <num>:<year>`|
| Official languages| English (primary), French (secondary)|
| Base vocabulary| NISO STS 1.2 (ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022) — unmodified|
| Document types| `recommendation`, `basic-publication`, `international-document`, `guide`, `expert-report`|
| Publication stages| WD → CD → DIS → FDIS → Published; OIML uses the NISO STS `@stage-code` values 30, 40, 50, 60 respectively.|
| Constraint over base (1 of 3)| `<permission>` required on any reused content. See Clause 5.|
| Constraint over base (2 of 3)| `<self-uri>` forbidden inside `<self-xref>`. See Clause 5.|
| Constraint over base (3 of 3)| `<title>` and `<pub-date>` required on every `<std>`. See Clause 5.|

The constraints over base are normative and apply to every OIML publication. They are restated and explained in Clause 5.

## 5Profile requirements over base NISO STS

## 5.1General

The profile specifies additional normative requirements over base NISO STS 1.2.

## 5.2Reused content shall carry `<permission>`

Any content reused by OIML from a source outside the OIML publication shall carry a `<permission>` element identifying the copyright holder and the license under which the content is reused.

**Why:** OIML’s editorial policy requires that readers can identify the
provenance and license of every reused passage. NISO STS permits but does not
require `<permission>`; OIML makes it mandatory for reused content.

NOTE

”Reused content” includes quotations, figures, tables, code samples, and any other material that OIML did not author. Content authored by OIML does not require `<permission>`.

## 5.3 `<self-uri>` shall not occur inside `<self-xref>`

The `<self-uri>` element shall not occur as a descendant of `<self-xref>`. The `@rid` attribute of `<self-xref>` is the only mechanism OIML permits for self-references inside an OIML publication.

**Why:** OIML’s rendering pipeline uses `@rid` to resolve internal cross references at parse time; permitting `<self-uri>` inside `<self-xref>` introduces two resolution paths and causes ambiguous link targets.

## 5.4Every `<std>` shall carry `<title>` and a dated designation

Every `<std>` element shall contain a `<title>`, and every `<std-ref>` within it shall declare datedness via `@type` ( `dated` when the designation embeds the publication year, e.g. `ISO 15223-1:2012`; `undated` otherwise). The publication year rides inside the dated `<std-ref>` designation — the base tag suite does not permit `<pub-date>` inside `<std>`.

**Why:** OIML bibliographic tooling renders citations by concatenating `<std-ref>` and `<title>`; omitting either the title or the datedness marker produces a malformed citation.

## 6Document structure

An OIML publication encoded in NISO STS is rooted at the `<standard>` element (or `<adoption>` for publications adopted from another SDO). The root contains three peer blocks plus an optional processing-metadata block:

```
<standard xml:lang="en">
  <processing-meta .../>      <!-- optional, NISO STS 1.2+ -->
  <front>...</front>          <!-- metadata, foreword, introduction -->
  <body>...</body>            <!-- clauses, tables, figures, formulae -->
  <back>...</back>            <!-- annexes, bibliography, indexes -->
</standard>
```

## 6.1Front matter

The OIML front matter contains an `<iso-meta>` block (used for compatibility with the wider STS ecosystem, even though OIML is not ISO), a foreword, and an introduction. For bilingual OIML publications, the secondary-language translation is carried in a sibling `<iso-meta xml:lang="fr">` block. See Clause 7 for the required metadata fields.

## 6.2Body

The body is built from nested `<sec>` elements. OIML clauses follow the
standard ISO/IEC structure (Scope, Normative references, Terms and
definitions, …​, main clauses, Annexes). Each `<sec>` carries a `<label>` and a
`<title>`.

NOTE

OIML uses machine-readable `@id` values for sections, not human-readable labels.

## 6.3Back matter

The OIML back matter holds:

- —
Annexes inside an `<app-group>`; each annex is an `<app>` with `@content-type` of `informative` or `normative`.

- —
The bibliography in a `<ref-list>` with `@content-type="bibliography"`.

- —
Indexes (optional) using `<index-div>` and `<index-entry>`.


Footnotes in OIML publications live at the point of use, not in `<back>` — see Clause 11.

## 8Body content

This clause specifies OIML’s conventions for prose content in the body of a publication.

## 8.1Paragraphs

Use `<p>` for paragraphs. OIML does not permit block-level structures inside `<p>`; nested structures must be siblings.

## 8.2Lists

Use `<list>` with one of these `@list-type` values:

`bullet`unordered list.
`order`numbered list with Arabic numerals.
`alpha-lower`, `alpha-upper`alphabetical.
`roman-lower`, `roman-upper`Roman numerals.
`arabic`added in NISO STS 1.2 for Arabic-numeral lists that do not fit `order`.

Each `<list-item>` may carry a `<label>`.

## 8.3Tables

Tables are wrapped in `<table-wrap>`. OIML uses the XHTML table model ( `<table>` with `<tr>`, `<td>`, `<th>`) by default. The model in use is declared on `<processing-meta>` via `@table-model`.

Table headers use `<th>` with `<bold>` for emphasis (harmonised with IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding2.1).

For detailed table-coding rules, see IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding2.1, Annex B.

## 8.4Figures

Figures are wrapped in `<fig>` with a `<label>`, `<caption>`, and one or more `<graphic>` elements. OIML requires `<alt-text>` on every figure for accessibility.

## 8.5Quotations

Block quotations use `<disp-quote>`. In NISO STS 1.2 (and OIML by extension), `<disp-quote>` may carry a source ( `<attrib>`) and usage permissions ( `<permissions>`).

## 8.6Notes and examples

OIML uses both normative and informative variants:

- —
`<normative-note>`, `<non-normative-note>`.

- —
`<normative-example>`, `<non-normative-example>`.


Notes inside tables, figures, and formulae use `<table-wrap-foot>` or `<caption>` as appropriate.

## 8.7Code and preformatted text

Block code uses `<code>` with `@code-type` and `@xml:space="preserve"`. Inline code uses `<inline-code>` (NISO STS 1.2). Verbatim text that is not code uses `<preformat>`.

## 9References and bibliography

OIML publications carry two reference lists in the back matter.

## 9.1Normative references

Encoded as a `<ref-list>` with `@content-type="normative-refs"`, typically inside `<front>` or as the first item in `<back>`. Each reference is held in a `<ref>` element wrapping a `<mixed-citation>` or `<element-citation>`.

## 9.2Bibliography

Encoded as a `<ref-list>` with `@content-type="bibliography"` in `<back>`.

## 9.3Citing other standards

References to other standards use the `<std>` element inside the citation. OIML places the following constraints over base NISO STS:

- —
Every `<std>` shall carry a `<title>`, and every `<std-ref>` within it shall declare datedness via `@type`. See Clause 5.

- —
`<std>` may carry `@use-type` to indicate whether the reference is dated, undated, or qualified (NISO STS 1.2 addition).


## 9.4Citing OIML’s own publications

When an OIML publication cites another OIML publication, the `<std>` element
carries the OIML designation in a `<std-ref>` with `@type="dated"` (e.g.,
`OIML R 7:1979`), followed by the publication’s `<title>`.

NOTE

OIML does not use punctuation between elements in `<ref-list>` — this is harmonised with the IEC practice from ed. 2.1 (see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §4.4.2).

## 10Mathematics, figures, and tables

## 10.1Mathematics

Inline mathematics use `<inline-formula>`; display (block) mathematics use `<disp-formula>`. OIML requires MathML 3.0 (declared on `<processing-meta>` via `@mathml="MathML 3.0"`).

```
<disp-formula id="eq_1">
  <label>(1)</label>
  <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
    ...
  </mml:math>
</disp-formula>
```

A formula key (legend) uses the `<legend>` element (NISO STS 1.2 addition — see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §7.3).

## 10.2Figures

Figures follow the conventions in Clause 8. The size of a graphic may be indicated in `@specific-use` (NISO STS 1.2 — see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §5.10).

Unit statements in figures: in OIML, the `<p>` containing the unit statement lives inside the figure caption ( `<caption>`) — harmonised with ed. 2.1 §8.4.

Sub-figures and multiple graphics: see the source coding guidelines §8.2 for the conventions OIML adopts.

## 10.3Tables

OIML tables use the XHTML table model by default. The full table-coding
conventions (alignment, merged cells, line breaks, lists inside cells,
landscape tables, rules, frames, border styling, alignment of the table, text
rotation) are inherited from the source coding guidelines Annex B.

NOTE

OIML harmonises with ISO/IEC ed. 2.1 on table styling (see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §6.3). Tables may carry size attributes for rendering information (see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §6.1).

## 11Indexing and navigation

## 11.1Tables of contents

The table of contents is generated from the section structure; it is not authored by hand. OIML rendering tooling produces the TOC from `<sec>`/ `<app>`  `<label>` and `<title>` pairs.

For author-controlled navigation aids (e.g., lists of figures, lists of tables), use a `<list-of>` element with the appropriate `@list-type`.

## 11.2Indexes

An author-created subject index lives in `<back>` inside an `<index-div>` tree. Each `<index-entry>` carries a `<term>` and optional `<see>` or `<see-also>` cross references, plus a target pointer ( `<xref>`).

## 11.3Internal cross-references

Internal cross-references use `<xref>` with `@rid` pointing at the target’s `@id`. The `@ref-type` attribute identifies the kind of target. OIML permits these `@ref-type` values:

- —
`sec` — section.

- —
`table` — table.

- —
`fig` — figure.

- —
`fn` — footnote.

- —
`bibr` — bibliographic entry.

- —
`abbreviation` — abbreviation (added in NISO STS 1.2; replaces the earlier `@ref-type="other"` practice).

- —
`custom` — with `@custom-type` of `note`, `term-entry`, or `example` (added in NISO STS 1.2).


For self-references within an OIML publication, the `<self-xref>` element is used; OIML resolves self-references via the `@rid` attribute only — see Clause 5 for the OIML-specific prohibition on `<self-uri>` inside `<self-xref>`.

## 11.4Footnotes

Footnote text in OIML lives at the point of use (inside the `<fn>` element), not collected in `<back>`. This is harmonised with the IEC/ISO Guidelines for Coding2.1, 10.1.8.

## **Annex A**  (Informative) **Examples**

## A.1General

This annex contains full XML examples of OIML publications encoded per this document.

## A.2Minimal OIML Recommendation

A minimal OIML Recommendation with a single clause and one bibliographic reference:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<standard xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"
          xml:lang="en"
          dtd-version="1.2">
  <processing-meta tagset-family="sts"
                   base-tagset="interchange"
                   table-model="xhtml"
                   mathml="MathML 3.0"
                   terminology-model="tbx"/>
  <front>
    <iso-meta>
      <std-ident>
        <originator>OIML</originator>
        <doc-type>r</doc-type>
        <doc-number>7</doc-number>
      </std-ident>
      <std-title-group>
        <title>Clinical thermometers (mercury-in-glass, with maximum device)</title>
      </std-title-group>
      <pub-date date-type="published">
        <day>01</day><month>01</month><year>1979</year>
      </pub-date>
      <release-version stage-code="60">Published</release-version>
      <permissions>
        <copyright-statement>© 1979 International Organization of Legal Metrology</copyright-statement>
        <copyright-year>1979</copyright-year>
        <copyright-holder>International Organization of Legal Metrology</copyright-holder>
      </permissions>
      <custom-meta-group>
        <custom-meta>
          <meta-name>oiml-doc-series</meta-name>
          <meta-value>R</meta-value>
        </custom-meta>
      </custom-meta-group>
    </iso-meta>
  </front>
  <body>
    <sec id="s_scope">
      <label>1</label>
      <title>Scope</title>
      <p>This Recommendation applies to clinical thermometers, mercury-in-glass,
        with maximum device.</p>
    </sec>
  </body>
  <back>
    <ref-list content-type="bibliography">
      <ref>
        <std type="dated">
          <std-ref type="dated">ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022</std-ref>,
          <title>STS: Standards Tag Suite (Version 1.2)</title>
        </std>
      </ref>
    </ref-list>
  </back>
</standard>
```

This example demonstrates:

- —
`<processing-meta>` declaring OIML’s default modeling choices.

- —
The required OIML metadata fields (identifier, title, pub-date, permissions).

- —
`stage-code="60"` indicating a published document.

- —
The OIML constraint of `<title>` plus a dated `<std-ref>` designation on `<std>` is satisfied.

- —
The OIML document-series letter ( `R`) carried in a `<custom-meta>`.


## A.3Bilingual OIML publication

For an OIML publication issued in both English and French, the metadata block is repeated with the appropriate `@xml:lang`:

```
<front>
  <iso-meta xml:lang="en">
    <std-ident>
      <originator>OIML</originator>
      <doc-type>r</doc-type>
      <doc-number>7</doc-number>
    </std-ident>
    <std-title-group>
      <title>Clinical thermometers (mercury-in-glass, with maximum device)</title>
    </std-title-group>
    ...
  </iso-meta>
  <iso-meta xml:lang="fr">
    <std-ident>
      <originator>OIML</originator>
      <doc-type>r</doc-type>
      <doc-number>7</doc-number>
    </std-ident>
    <std-title-group>
      <title>Thermomètres médicaux (à mercure, en verre, avec dispositif à maximum)</title>
    </std-title-group>
    ...
  </iso-meta>
</front>
```

## **Annex B**  (Informative) **Element map**

This annex lists every NISO STS element that OIML uses, with a one-line note on OIML’s convention for each. For the full normative description of each element, see the Tag Library entry linked from the element name.

Table B.1 — Element usage summary

| Element| OIML usage|
| ---| ---|
| `<standard>`| Root element for every OIML publication that is not an adoption.|
| `<adoption>`| Root element when OIML adopts another SDO’s publication.|
| `<iso-meta>`| Header metadata block. OIML uses `<iso-meta>` for compatibility with the wider NISO STS ecosystem.|
| `<std-ident>`| The OIML identifier, decomposed: `<originator>OIML</originator>` plus `<doc-type>` (series letter), `<doc-number>`, and `<part-number>` where applicable (e.g. `OIML R 7:1979` → doc-type `r`, doc-number `7`).|
| `<std>`| Bibliographic reference to a standard. OIML requires `<title>` and a dated or undated `<std-ref>` designation — see Clause 5.|
| `<title>`| Required on `<std>`; primary title of a document or section.|
| `<std-ref>`| Required on `<std>`; the standard’s designation, with `@type="dated"` when it embeds the publication year and `@type="undated"` otherwise.|
| `<permission>`| Required on reused content — see Clause 5.|
| `<self-xref>`| Self-reference within the publication. OIML resolves via `@rid` only.|
| `<self-uri>`| Forbidden as a descendant of `<self-xref>` — see Clause 5.|
| `<p>`| Paragraph — base prose unit.|
| `<list>`| List (ordered or unordered).|
| `<table-wrap>`| Table wrapper.|
| `<fig>`| Figure wrapper; `<alt-text>` is required by OIML editorial policy.|
| `<xref>`| Cross-reference; OIML uses `@ref-type` from the NISO STS controlled vocabulary.|
| `<fn>`| Footnote; lives at point of use per OIML convention.|
| `<disp-formula>` / `<inline-formula>`| Display and inline mathematics; OIML uses MathML 3.0.|
| `<sec>`| Section; nested for sub-clauses.|
| `<app-group>` / `<app>`| Annex group and annex entries.|
| `<ref-list>`| Reference list (normative or bibliographic).|
| `<contrib-group>` / `<contrib>`| Contributor group; used for TC/SC attribution.|

This annex is informative. The authoritative reference for every element is the corresponding chapter in the NISO STS Tag Library.

**Answer to your question:** `<std-ident>` is part of the NISO STS standard itself ([Z39.102-2022](https://www.niso-sts.org/TagLibrary/niso-sts-TL-1-2-html/element/std-ident.html), in both `<std-meta>` and `<iso-meta>`) and matches ISO's own usage. The OIML invention was `<doc-identifier>` — it exists in neither NISO STS 1.2 nor ISO STS (the ISO-only element is `<doc-ident>`, which NISO says non-ISO orgs shouldn't use). The same audit exposed that `<std-ident>` and `<pub-date>` are not permitted inside `<std>`, which made the old clause 5.4 unsatisfiable and failed the converter against its own validator on every reference.

**Fixed across both repos:**

- **metanorma-oiml** (PR #16, commits `96599a9`, `ed9bdd5`): identifier decomposed into `<std-ident>` (`originator`/`doc-type`/`doc-number`/`part-number`), `<pub-date>` actually emitted (was silently dropped), `xml:lang` restored on `<standard>` (attribute was set under the wrong name), citations carry the year in `<std-ref type="dated">`, validator rule aligned to NISO STS with the correct 5.4 reference, stale specs rewritten to the current API. **74 + 158 specs green; converter output validates clean.**
- **oimlsmart/specs** (PRs [#7](https://github.com/oimlsmart/specs/pull/7), [#8](https://github.com/oimlsmart/specs/pull/8), rebase-merged): X 999's Table 2, clause 5.4, §9, Table 3, element map, and Annex A examples now specify the conformant encoding.
- **Deployments verified live**: both GHA runs succeeded and the live page now shows the corrected 5.4 text, the `<std-ident>` examples, and the fixed Table 1 constraint.

125	            Array(note_obj.ul).each { |ul| content << list_transformer.transform(ul) }
126	            Array(note_obj.ol).each { |ol| content << list_transformer.transform(ol) }
127	          end
128	
129	          def build_list(list, list_type)
130	            list_transformer.transform_with_type(list, list_type)
131	          end
132	
133	          def add_sources(content, source_term)
134	            Array(source_term.source).each { |s| content << build_source(s) }
135	          end
136	
137	          def build_source(source)
138	            origin = source.origin
139	            return nil unless origin
140	
141	            citeas = origin.citeas
142	            locality = extract_locality(origin)
143	            ordinal = bib_ordinal(origin)
144	
145	            text = "[SOURCE: #{citeas}"
146	            if locality
147	              text << ", #{locality}"
148	              text << "[#{ordinal}]" if ordinal
149	              text << " "
150	            end
151	            text << "]"
152	            ::Sts::IsoSts::Paragraph.new(content: [text])
153	          end
154	
155	          def extract_locality(origin)
156	            ls_arr = origin.locality_stack
157	            return nil unless ls_arr.is_a?(Array) && ls_arr.any?
158	
159	            parts = []
160	            ls_arr.each do |ls|
161	              Array(ls.bib_locality).each do |loc|
162	                from = loc.reference_from
163	                val = case from
164	                      when String then from
165	                      when nil then ""
166	                      else
167	                        cv = from.content rescue nil
168	                        cv ? Array(cv).first.to_s : from.to_s
169	                      end
170	                parts << val if val && !val.empty?
171	              end
172	            end
173	            parts.empty? ? nil : parts.join(", ")
174	          end
175	
176	          def bib_ordinal(origin)
177	            bibitemid = origin.bibitemid
178	            return nil unless bibitemid
179	
180	            bib = context.source.typed_root.bibliography
181	            return nil unless bib
182	
183	            items = Array(bib.references).flat_map { |rs| Array(rs.references) }
184	            items.each_with_index do |item, i|
185	              return (i + 1).to_s if item.id == bibitemid || item.anchor == bibitemid
186	            end
187	            nil
188	          end
189	        end
190	      end
191	    end
192	  end
193	end
