# outputs (metanorma-oiml). Kept separate from the compile Gemfile because the
# pubid 2.0 / relaton prerelease line cannot coexist with the released
# metanorma-cli stack (metanorma-standoc pins relaton-cli ~> 2.1.0, and
# RubyGems never satisfies a non-prerelease requirement with a prerelease).
#
# Usage:
#   git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/metanorma/metanorma-oiml vendor/metanorma-oiml
#   BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.renderer bundle install
#   BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.renderer bundle exec ruby -e '...'
#   BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.renderer bundle exec oiml-sts convert ...

source "https://rubygems.org"

# >= 0.2.11 renders the document body; earlier releases emit an empty page
gem "metanorma-document", "~> 0.2.12"
# path source (not git): clone first —
#   git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/metanorma/metanorma-oiml vendor/metanorma-oiml
gem "metanorma-oiml", path: "vendor/metanorma-oiml"

# required at load time by metanorma-document but only declared transitively
gem "mml"

# pubid 2.0 / relaton prerelease line (explicit pre-segment requirements are
# what allow Bundler to select prereleases)
gem "pubid", "~> 2.0.0.pre.alpha"
gem "relaton-bib", "2.2.0.pre.alpha.1"
Gemfile
LICENSE
README.adoc


</details>

```ruby
def build_table_note_foot(source_table)
  return nil unless source_table.class.method_defined?(:note)
  notes = Array(source_table.note)
  return nil if notes.empty?

  nn_notes = notes.map { |n| build_niso_note(n) }.compact
  return nil if nn_notes.empty?
  ::Sts::TbxIsoTml::TableWrapFoot.new(non_normative_note: nn_notes)
end

def build_niso_note(source_note)
  paragraphs = note_paragraphs(source_note)
  return nil if paragraphs.empty?
  ::Sts::NisoSts::NonNormativeNote.new(p: paragraphs)
end
```

```ruby
def partition_content(content)
  paragraphs = content.grep(::Sts::IsoSts::Paragraph)
  lists = content.grep(::Sts::IsoSts::List)
  notes = content.grep(::Sts::IsoSts::NonNormativeNote)
  others = content.reject { |c| c.is_a?(::Sts::IsoSts::Paragraph) || c.is_a?(::Sts::IsoSts::List) || c.is_a?(::Sts::IsoSts::NonNormativeNote) }
  [paragraphs + others, lists, notes]
end
```

        # Apply nil marker for empty scalar value
        def apply_nil_marker_for_empty(element, rule)
          to_map = (rule.option(:value_map) || {})[:to] || {}
          if to_map[:empty] == :nil
            element.xsi_nil = true
          end
        end

        # Apply content to element (text or raw)
        #
        # @param element [XmlElement] The element
        # @param text [String] The text content
        # @param rule [CompiledRule] The rule
        def apply_element_content(element, text, rule)
          if rule.raw
            # Store as raw content for adapter serialization
            element.raw_content = text.to_s
          else
            # Normal text content - will be escaped by adapter
            element.text_content = text
          end

          # Apply cdata flag if set on the rule
          element.cdata = rule.cdata if rule.cdata
        end
      end

        def self.from_model(sc, renderer:)
          id = renderer.safe_attr(sc, :id)
          lang = renderer.safe_attr(sc, :lang)

          name_html = if sc.name
                        renderer.render_inline_element(sc.name)
                      end

          code_text = if sc.body&.content
                        Array(sc.body.content).join
                      elsif sc.content
                        Array(sc.content).join
                      else
                        ""
                      end
          raw_text = code_text.gsub("&lt;", "<").gsub("&gt;", ">").gsub("&amp;", "&").gsub(
            "&quot;", "\""
          )

          new(
            id: id,
            lang: lang,
            name_html: name_html,
            code_html: renderer.escape_html(raw_text),
            css_class: "sourcecode",
          )
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

All done. Summary of the parity validation and the root-cause fix:

## Parity validation result

Using your parity validator against a **freshly generated** metanorma-document HTML (the old `document.html` was stale — the doc's `:mn-output-extensions:` excludes html, and the site HTML comes from the metanorma-document stage):

**PASS — 0 missing headings, paragraphs, table cells, list items, notes, images; 100% paragraph coverage, 96.7% word coverage** (the residual ~3% is marker-gluing tokens like `-authors` and the render timestamp, not content).

Gaps found and fixed along the way (metanorma-oiml, pushed to PR #16 as `2745660` + `67dc7a8`):
- Terms lost their numbers (`3.1`) and term notes were text-prefixed paragraphs — now `<non-normative-note>` with `Note 1 to entry:` labels.
- Normative refs were numbered `[1]–[5]` (ISO leaves them unnumbered; only bibliography gets labels); `std-ref`/`title` now join with the NISO `", "` idiom; originator noise dropped.
- Table notes were silently dropped — now dispatched as table siblings; refs render as paragraphs with the label inside.
- **Sourcecode blocks were silently dropped entirely** (routed to the note transformer), then came back empty, then double-escaped.
- Annex headings show `Annex A`; notes/examples carry kind labels; parity normaliser fixes (nbsp-before-number-strip, annex obligations, `.h-anchor`, notes as a first-class set).

## The root cause you suspected

Confirmed and fixed in metanorma-document ([PR #33](https://github.com/metanorma/metanorma-document/pull/33)): `SourcecodeBody`'s `map_all_content` keeps content **markup-encoded** (`&lt;`) for roundtrip fidelity, so every text consumer must decode. Your own `SourcecodeDrop` did it with a `gsub` chain that misses numeric refs; the mirror handler didn't decode at all; my transformer double-escaped. Now `SourcecodeBody#decoded_content` unwraps entities once (comments stay literal), both consumers use it, with a new spec proving decode + roundtrip. metanorma-oiml's preformat uses `decoded_content` with a local decode as fallback until 0.3.1 ships — so it works against both the released 0.3.0 and your repo.

One caveat: the full metanorma-document suite is still running in the background (heavy roundtrip fixtures); the 422 examples covering every touched file pass. I'll flag it if it surfaces anything when it completes.

module Metanorma
  module Document
    class CLI
      class Error < StandardError; end

      ToMirrorOptions = Struct.new(
        :xml_path,
        :output,
        :flavor,
        :id_strategy,
        :title,
        keyword_init: true,
      )

      ToHtmlOptions = Struct.new(
        :xml_path,
        :output,
        :flavor,
        keyword_init: true,
      )

      def self.run(argv)
        command = argv.shift
        case command
        when "to-mirror"
...
        raise Error, "XML path required" unless xml_path
        raise Error, "File not found: #{xml_path}" unless File.exist?(xml_path)

        options.xml_path = xml_path
        options
      end

      def self.execute_to_html(options)
        # Metanorma::Html is autoloaded from metanorma/document.
        # Reuse the mirror pipeline's flavor inference/model dispatch so
        # to-html and to-mirror parse documents identically.
        step = Mirror::Output::Pipeline::Steps::ParseXml.new
        flavor = options.flavor || step.infer_flavor(options.xml_path)
        doc = step.flavor_class(flavor).from_xml(File.read(options.xml_path))
        write_output(Html::Generator.generate(doc), options.output)
      end

      def self.usage
        <<~USAGE
          Usage: metanorma-document <command> [options]

          Commands:
            to-mirror    Convert presentation XML to mirror JSON

3	# MathML passthrough helper.
4	#
5	# Design note: previously this module extracted plain text from MathML via
6	# regex symbol rules, subscript/superscript rewriting, and asciimath
7	# conversion. That approach was wrong — mnconvert (the production
8	# Metanorma→STS converter) copies MathML verbatim into <inline-formula>.
9	# We do the same via Mml::V3::Math.from_xml + Sts::IsoSts::InlineFormula.
10	#
11	# The text-extraction methods (asciimath_to_plain_text, mathml_to_plain_text,
12	# apply_symbol_rules, apply_subscript_rules, apply_superscript_rules) were
13	# removed. No code should reach back into this module for math rendering —
14	# inline/dispatched formulas pass MathML through structurally.
15	module Metanorma
16	  module Oiml
17	    module Sts
18	      module MathmlBuilder
19	        module_function
20	
21	        MATHML_NS = "http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"
22	
23	        def wrap_math_content(content)
24	          "<math xmlns='#{MATHML_NS}'>#{content}</math>"
25	        end
26	
27	        # Builds a math model instance from a stem-bearing typed model node.
28	        # Handles StemInlineElement (.math), StemBlockElement (.math),
29	        # and FmtStemElement (.semx[].math). Returns nil when the node
30	        # carries no parseable MathML — callers should silently drop
31	        # the formula in that case (mnconvert's behavior).
32	        #
33	        # `klass:` selects which typed Math model to instantiate.
34	        # Defaults to Mml::V3::Math (used by Sts::IsoSts::* models).
35	        # Pass ::Sts::TbxIsoTml::Math when targeting Sts::NisoSts::*
36	        # models (e.g. Sts::TbxIsoTml::Td cells).
37	        def math_from_stem(stem_node, klass: Mml::V3::Math)
38	          math_el = first_math_element(stem_node)
39	          return nil unless math_el
40	          return nil unless math_el.class.method_defined?(:content)
41	
42	          content = math_el.content
43	          return nil if content.nil?
44	
45	          string = content.to_s
46	          return nil if string.empty?
47	
48	          klass.from_xml(wrap_math_content(string))
49	        rescue StandardError
50	          nil
51	        end
52	
53	        # Wraps the stem's MathML in an InlineFormula for
54	        # use inside paragraphs and table cells. Returns nil if the
55	        # stem carries no parseable MathML.
56	        #
57	        # Always uses Mml::V3::Math — the mml gem preserves all
58	        # MathML elements (mtext, mrow, msub, etc.) during roundtrip,
59	        # unlike Sts::TbxIsoTml::Math which drops elements inside
60	        # <mstyle>.
61	        def inline_formula_from_stem(stem_node, klass: ::Sts::IsoSts::InlineFormula)
62	          math = math_from_stem(stem_node, klass: Mml::V3::Math)
63	          return nil unless math
64	
65	          klass.new(math: math)
66	        end
67	
68	        # SemanticMathElement is a subclass of Mml::V3::Math — already
69	        # a fully-typed Math model. The earlier stringify/re-parse path
70	        # broke because SemanticMathElement doesn't expose a `.content`
71	        # accessor at the Lutaml level.
72	        def first_math_element(stem_node)
73	          if stem_node.is_a?(Metanorma::Document::Components::Inline::FmtStemElement)
74	            Array(stem_node.semx).flat_map { |semx| Array(semx.math) }.first
75	          elsif stem_node.class.method_defined?(:math)
76	            Array(stem_node.math).first
77	          end
78	        end
79	
80	        def math_from_stem(stem_node, klass: Mml::V3::Math)
81	          math_el = first_math_element(stem_node)
82	          return nil unless math_el
83	
84	          # The stem's `math` attribute already carries a typed MML model
85	          # (SemanticMathElement inherits Mml::V3::Math). Passing it
86	          # straight through avoids the earlier stringify-and-reparse
87	          # roundtrip — which depended on `math_el.content` and broke
88	          # when the typed model changed shape.
89	          return math_el if math_el.is_a?(klass)
90	
91	          # Fallback for any future stem shape that isn't already an
92	          # Mml::V3::Math subclass: build from its serialized XML.
93	          string = math_el.to_s
94	          return nil if string.empty?
95	
96	          klass.from_xml(wrap_math_content(string))
97	        rescue StandardError
98	          nil
99	        end
100	      end
101	    end
102	  end
103	end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Metanorma
  module Html
    module Drops
      class ExampleDrop < BlockElementDrop
        def self.from_model(example, renderer:)
          id = renderer.safe_attr(example, :id)
          label = renderer.extract_block_label(example, "EXAMPLE")

          content_html = renderer.render_full_block_children(example) || ""

          new(
            id: id,
            label_html: renderer.escape_html(label),
            content_html: content_html,
            css_class: "example",
          )
        end
      end
    end
  end
end
